newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany plans no tax increases - Gerhardt.
newsitem.headline: Germany plans no tax increases - Gerhardt.

text.p: Germany's ruling coalition decided no tax increases would be needed to plug a spending gap foreseen for 1997, Wolfgang Gerhardt, chairman of junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP) said on Friday.

Coalition sources said earlier the coalition had agreed in meetings on Friday morning to delay a planned cut in the solidarity surcharge on income taxes. The talks also considered a possible rise in the petroleum tax.
"There are no tax increases," Gerhardt told journalists.

FDP general secretary Guido Westerwelle said at the same news conference the solidarity surcharge would remain uncut in 1997, meaning that a reduction planned for January to 6.5 percent from the current 7.5 percent would not take place.
The government had considered raising the petroleum tax to help plug a 1997 spending gap estimated at about 10 billion marks. But the plan ran into broad popular opposition.
